# Chat submission and published static assets — 2026-10-24

The initial deployment returned HTTP 200 for JavaScript and stylesheets but served empty bodies. The page's prerendered HTML appeared, while the missing Blazor runtime meant typing could not enable Send. The deployment checks inspected status codes without verifying asset contents, and the initial production browser check consequently missed the inactive page.

The systemd service starts in `/srv/secondbrain`. The application previously inherited that directory as its content root, although published web assets live beside the binaries in `/usr/local/lib/secondbrain/wwwroot`. `Program.cs` now explicitly uses `AppContext.BaseDirectory` as the application content root. A regression checks the actual hosted environment, and the upgrade verifier now requires nonempty JavaScript/CSS/icon responses that exactly match installed files, including `/_framework/blazor.web.js`.

An isolated production static-asset host reproduced the failure with the same published manifest: the unrelated working directory returned HTTP 200 with zero bytes; the application directory returned all 200,645 bytes of the Blazor runtime. All 245 server tests and 18 deployment/setup safeguard tests passed.

The fix was [deployed successfully](evidence/m2-static-fix-20261024/deployment-result.json) through the managed service at 18:14 UTC on 2026-10-24. All 427 installed files matched the release. [Independent LAN checks](evidence/m2-static-fix-20261024/installed-verification.json) verified that the script, styles, and icon exactly matched the installed nonempty files. The [LAN browser](evidence/m2-static-fix-20261024/lan-browser.json) loaded the Blazor runtime and completed transport negotiation; its [console](evidence/m2-static-fix-20261024/lan-browser-console.txt) confirmed a WebSocket connection without errors. The existing account, credentials, configuration, key ring, and document were preserved. This production browser check was signed out; the authenticated chat workflow remains covered by the earlier live-provider qualification and server tests.

The user also requested deployment without repeated sudo handoffs. The [managed deployment setup](../../deploy/systemd/managed-deployment.md) limits the passwordless command to starting a fixed, root-owned deployment service. The user completed the one-time setup and the agent performed this deployment without an interactive password.
